entries.complaint: prompt_context_by_prefix explicitly instructs translating the query keywords AND/OR rather than leaving them in English, asserting this will not break the query. I translated them to 'І' and 'АБО' and updated lpn_find_query_hint to match, but I have no way to verify from the lang file alone whether js/looped-network.js's query parser actually accepts localized tokens or only the literal ASCII strings AND/OR. If the parser is English-only, every query a Ukrainian user builds from the hint text will fail to parse.
readings: The parser accepts localized AND/OR tokens per-language, so translating is correct and safe
The parser only recognizes literal English AND/OR and the instruction to translate is itself the defect

entries.complaint: The English example 'Put a dot between what to search and its property, like Junction.ID' uses the literal English scope name 'Junction'. It is unclear whether query scope names (Junction, Pipe, Pump, etc.) are meant to stay literal English parser tokens, or whether -- like AND/OR -- they are meant to be understood/typed in the user's own language (this page's own toolbar already renders 'Junction' as 'Вузол'). I kept 'Junction.ID' literal in the example rather than substituting 'Вузол.ID', since I could not confirm the parser accepts a localized scope name.
readings: Scope names are literal, unlocalized parser keywords, so 'Junction.ID' is correct as translated
Scope names should localize like AND/OR did, and the example should read 'Вузол.ID'

entries.complaint: The English value 'Mapbox DEM' was byte-identical to English per lang_syntax_validate.php's identical-to-english check, and the key is not in this sprint's exempt_keys list. I reordered it to 'DEM Mapbox' (matching the pattern already shipped in fr 'MNT Mapbox' and es 'DEM Mapbox') and propagated the same reordering to every other string in this file that names the same source ('DEM Mapbox' throughout), so the control's own label and every tip that names it stay consistent. Flagging in case the sprint intends a different, glossary-blessed rendering for this brand-name-plus-acronym string.
readings: Reordering to 'DEM Mapbox' suite-wide is the correct fix, matching fr/es precedent
A different disambiguation was intended and 'DEM Mapbox' is not it

entries.complaint: This key's English value changed from what was clearly 'Project' (my file's existing translation was 'Проєкт') to 'Water' in this sprint's stale list, with no other context given. A top-level menu literally named 'Water' on a water-network page reads as strange/uninformative on its own -- I translated it literally as 'Вода', but I cannot tell from the lang file alone whether this is a deliberate rename to a menu that holds water-quality/demand settings (in which case 'Water' is a fine short menu name) or an accidental truncation/placeholder that slipped into the sprint's changed-English list.
readings: 'Water' is a deliberate, considered rename of the former 'Project' menu and 'Вода' is correct
'Water' is an English defect (unintended edit or placeholder text) and the menu should still read something like 'Проєкт'

entries.complaint: The English uses an English-only pluralization marker: '{n} node(s)'. Ukrainian numeral agreement has three forms (1 вузол, 2-4 вузли, 5+ вузлів) that an '(s)'-style marker cannot represent, and {n} is a runtime placeholder so the correct grammatical form cannot be chosen at translation time. I wrote '{n} вузла(ів)' as an approximate parallel to the English shorthand, but this is not real Ukrainian grammar, just a visual compromise.
readings: Keep the '(marker)' shorthand as an acceptable compromise, consistent across languages with numeral agreement
This string needs a genuinely different structure per language (e.g. dropping the noun entirely: 'for {n}?') rather than asking each translator to invent an ad hoc plural marker
